capabilities: Read the current note aloud sentence by sentence with a local Piper voice
Highlight and scroll to the sentence being read in the editor and reading view
Download Piper voices in 58 languages from the settings
Control playback with commands and status bar buttons (pause, resume, next/previous sentence and paragraph)
Adjust speed, sentence length, and paragraph pauses in settings
extras: Desktop only (Windows, macOS, Linux); does not work on phones or tablets. Requires the free, open-source calibre app installed outside the vault. Voice downloads come from huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices; reading itself works offline and no notes are sent anywhere. Step-by-step setup lives in HELP.md, also available via the Help command inside Obsidian. The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to listen to a note read aloud, so users must leave the app or rely on cloud TTS services.

relations.evidence: The speaking is done by the Piper built into calibre (8.8 or newer)
Read Aloud starts calibre's calibre-debug in the background to run the speech engine

summary: Text-to-speech reader that reads notes aloud sentence by sentence with a local Piper voice, highlighting the sentence currently being read.
